authors: Simão AY; Rosado T; Barroso M; Andraus M; Gallardo E

exposure_or_policy: Festival attendance; self-reported substance use assessed across timeframes from same-day use to lifetime use
population: Adult international music festival attendees in Portugal
setting: International music festival in Portugal, July 2022 and July 2023
public_health_measure: Self-reported substance use prevalence and recency
study_design: Anonymous self-administered cross-sectional questionnaire with voluntary hair sample collection
estimate_value: Lifetime self-reported use: alcohol 96%, cannabinoids 90%, cocaine 56.6%, and MDMA 77.5%. Same-day use: alcohol 32.5%, cigarettes 39.0%, cannabinoids 14.9%, cocaine 0.8%, and MDMA 0.4%.
effect_or_statistic: Descriptive percentages
association_or_trend: Alcohol and cannabinoids were most commonly reported overall; cannabinoid use was more recent than use of cocaine and MDMA.
time_window: Questionnaire timeframes ranged from the day of the survey to more than one year ago; cumulative percentages represent any reported use across timeframes.
finding_summary: Among festival attendees, alcohol and cannabinoids had the highest cumulative self-reported use. Cannabinoid use was notably recent, while same-day cocaine and MDMA use was uncommon.
evidence_location: Results, Substance Use History by Group; Table 1
compound: Festival attendance; self-reported substance use assessed across timeframes from same-day use to lifetime use
support: Among festival attendees, alcohol and cannabinoids had the highest cumulative self-reported use. Cannabinoid use was notably recent, while same-day cocaine and MDMA use was uncommon.
follow_up_duration: Questionnaire timeframes ranged from the day of the survey to more than one year ago; cumulative percentages represent any reported use across timeframes.
effect_size: Descriptive percentages
result_direction: Alcohol and cannabinoids were most commonly reported overall; cannabinoid use was more recent than use of cocaine and MDMA.

population: Adult international music festival attendees who provided hair samples
setting: International music festival in Portugal, July 2022 and July 2023
public_health_measure: Hair toxicology positivity and detected compounds
study_design: Cross-sectional survey combined with quantitative hair analysis by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry
estimate_value: 125/249 (50%) samples were positive for at least one substance. Detected: benzoylecgonine 61 (24.5%), MDMA 60 (24.1%), ketamine 57 (22.9%), cocaine 46 (18.5%), and cannabinoids 52 (20.9%).
effect_or_statistic: Descriptive counts and percentages
association_or_trend: MDMA, ketamine, cocaine, and cannabinoid-related compounds were commonly detected; hair positivity reflects incorporation over the analysed hair length, which varied across participants.
time_window: Drug incorporation over the analysed hair length; retrospective period was not standardized across participants.
finding_summary: Half of the festival attendees' hair samples tested positive for at least one analysed substance. follow_up_duration: Drug incorporation over the analysed hair length; retrospective period was not standardized across participants.
effect_size: Descriptive counts and percentages

exposure_or_policy: Self-reported substance use compared with positive hair toxicology for the same substance
population: Adult international music festival attendees completing the questionnaire and providing hair samples
setting: International music festival in Portugal
public_health_measure: Association and agreement between self-report and hair toxicology
study_design: Cross-sectional comparison of questionnaire responses and quantitative hair toxicology
estimate_value: Odds of hair positivity among self-reported users: cocaine OR 7.53 (95% CI 3.39–16.70), ketamine OR 5.22 (2.49–10.92), and MDMA OR 4.07 (1.54–10.73). No significant association for cannabinoids (OR 1.06, 0.38–2.98). Among self-reported non-users, odds of hair positivity were lower for cocaine (OR 0.13, 0.06–0.30), ketamine (OR 0.19, 0.09–0.40), and MDMA (OR 0.25, 0.09–0.65).
effect_or_statistic: Odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals
association_or_trend: Self-reported use was significantly associated with hair positivity for cocaine, ketamine, and MDMA, but not cannabinoids. Agreement among reported users was limited: 37.6% for cocaine, 34.1% for ketamine, 28.5% for MDMA, and 21.0% for cannabis.
time_window: Questionnaire use history covered multiple timeframes; hair detection covered a participant-dependent analysed hair length.
finding_summary: Self-report and hair toxicology showed significant associations for cocaine, ketamine, and MDMA, but agreement among reported users was low, especially for cannabis. The authors identify differences in reporting and non-standardized hair detection windows as possible contributors to discrepancies.
evidence_location: Results, Comparison of Self-Reported Drug Use and Quantitative Hair Analysis; Tables 2, 3, and 5
compound: Self-reported substance use compared with positive hair toxicology for the same substance

authors: Frederic Béen; Erik Emke; João Matias; Jose Antonio Baz‐Lomba; Tim Boogaerts; Sara Castiglioni; Marina Celia Campos‐Mañas; Alberto Celma; Adrian Covaci; Pim de Voogt; Félix Hernández; Barbara Kasprzyk‐Hordern; Thomas L. ter Laak; Malcolm J. Reid; Noelia Salgueiro‐González; Ruud Steenbeek; Alexander L.N. van Nuijs; Ettore Zuccato; Lubertus Bijlsma
exposure_or_policy: Early COVID-19 lockdown restrictions; wastewater drug-residue loads in 2020 compared with previous years, particularly 2019.
population: Population-level drug use represented by wastewater from seven European city catchments: Amsterdam, Utrecht, Eindhoven, Brussels, Boom, Milan, and Castellon.
setting: Influent wastewater at wastewater treatment plants in the Netherlands, Belgium, Italy, and Spain.
public_health_measure: Wastewater-derived population-normalized amphetamine (AMP) loads.
study_design: Wastewater analysis comparing 2020 population-normalized drug-residue loads with yearly monitoring data from previous years.
estimate_value: Amsterdam: AMP decreased almost 50% versus 2019, to levels comparable with 2017. Utrecht, Brussels, and Boom: no decrease versus 2019; the recent increasing trend appeared to continue. AMP was not detected or only sporadically detected in Castellon and Milan.
effect_or_statistic: One-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum tests: Utrecht, Brussels, and Boom p < 0.05; Amsterdam p > 0.05.
estimate_unit: Population-normalized mass load (mg/day per 1,000 inhabitants); percentage change where reported.
association_or_trend: AMP trends during early lockdowns varied by city; there was no uniform decrease.
time_window: Wastewater sampled March–May 2020; comparisons with previous years, including 2019.
finding_summary: Wastewater AMP loads showed heterogeneous changes across cities during early lockdowns: Amsterdam had an approximately 50% decrease, while Utrecht, Brussels, and Boom showed no decrease and the prior increasing trend appeared to persist. AMP was too infrequent or absent for comparison in Castellon and Milan.
evidence_location: Results, Yearly trends
compound: Early COVID-19 lockdown restrictions; wastewater drug-residue loads in 2020 compared with previous years, particularly 2019.
support: Wastewater AMP loads showed heterogeneous changes across cities during early lockdowns: Amsterdam had an approximately 50% decrease, while Utrecht, Brussels, and Boom showed no decrease and the prior increasing trend appeared to persist. follow_up_duration: Wastewater sampled March–May 2020; comparisons with previous years, including 2019.
effect_size: One-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum tests: Utrecht, Brussels, and Boom p < 0.05; Amsterdam p > 0.05.
result_direction: AMP trends during early lockdowns varied by city; there was no uniform decrease.

study_title: Changes in drug use in European cities during early COVID-19 lockdowns - A snapshot from wastewater analysis.
authors: Frederic Béen; Erik Emke; João Matias; Jose Antonio Baz‐Lomba; Tim Boogaerts; Sara Castiglioni; Marina Celia Campos‐Mañas; Alberto Celma; Adrian Covaci; Pim de Voogt; Félix Hernández; Barbara Kasprzyk‐Hordern; Thomas L. ter Laak; Malcolm J. Reid; Noelia Salgueiro‐González; Ruud Steenbeek; Alexander L.N. van Nuijs; Ettore Zuccato; Lubertus Bijlsma
exposure_or_policy: Early COVID-19 lockdown restrictions; weekly wastewater drug-residue patterns in 2020 compared with 2018 and 2019.
population: Population-level drug-use patterns represented by daily wastewater loads in the monitored European city catchments.
setting: Influent wastewater at wastewater treatment plants in the Netherlands, Belgium, Italy, and Spain.
public_health_measure: Changes in weekly patterns and weekend peaks in population-normalized loads of AMP, BE, MDMA, METH, and THC-COOH.
study_design: Wastewater analysis comparing weekly drug-residue patterns from 2018–2020.
estimate_value: No generalized change in weekly patterns; changes differed by substance and city. Examples included absent or less pronounced weekend peaks for AMP, BE, and MDMA in Amsterdam, and a substantially lower Milan MDMA weekend peak in 2020 than in 2018 and 2019.
association_or_trend: Weekly patterns remained heterogeneous across cities and substances.
time_window: Weekly patterns observed in 2018–2020, including wastewater samples collected during March–May 2020.
finding_summary: The study found no general shift in weekly drug-load patterns during early lockdowns. Some cities showed changed or less pronounced weekend peaks, while patterns in other city-substance combinations remained largely unchanged; results varied across locations and substances.
evidence_location: Results, Weekly patterns
compound: Early COVID-19 lockdown restrictions; weekly wastewater drug-residue patterns in 2020 compared with 2018 and 2019.
support: The study found no general shift in weekly drug-load patterns during early lockdowns. Some cities showed changed or less pronounced weekend peaks, while patterns in other city-substance combinations remained largely unchanged; results varied across locations and substances.

effect_size: No generalized change in weekly patterns; changes differed by substance and city. Examples included absent or less pronounced weekend peaks for AMP, BE, and MDMA in Amsterdam, and a substantially lower Milan MDMA weekend peak in 2020 than in 2018 and 2019.
